cases.name: Dargah Hazrat Syed Asadullah Shah Quadri Shaheed (Neknampur Dargah Sadullah)
cases.status: Ongoing; waqf land attached to the 400-year-old dargah has shrunk from roughly 60 acres to about 1-2 acres. A Waqf Board task force intervened in September 2025 but encroachment claims continue; multiple representations and High Court petitions filed by the Mutawalli have not stopped land grabbers.
cases.court_case: Petitions filed in Telangana High Court by the Mutawalli (case details not specified in sources)
cases.summary: Waqf land at survey nos. 52, 61, 62, 63 and 166 attached to this 400-year-old dargah has been progressively encroached since 2005-06 by private developers and land grabbers using fake pattas; separately, 60 acres of the same waqf land were allotted by the government in 2012 for an 850-house AP Secretariat employees' colony.

cases.name: Dargah Hazrat Hussain Shah Wali (Manikonda Jagir land)
cases.estimated_value_inr: Rs 32,000 crore (2012 HC estimate); Rs 81,614 crore cited in a separate report
cases.status: The 2012 Andhra Pradesh High Court ruling declaring the land Waqf property was overturned by the Supreme Court in 2022, which held the land belongs to the Telangana state government.
cases.court_case: Manikonda Jagir case; AP High Court (2012) reversed by Supreme Court of India (2022)
cases.summary: 1,654 acres of prime Manikonda land allotted by the state government to IT/MNC firms was declared Waqf property of Dargah Hussain Shah Wali by the Andhra Pradesh High Court in 2012 (valuing it at Rs 32,000 crore), but the Supreme Court set aside that ruling in 2022 and awarded the land to the state government and TGIIC.

cases.name: Lanco Hills Technology Park land
cases.estimated_value_inr: Part of the Rs 32,000 crore Manikonda land valuation
cases.status: Company built residential/commercial towers instead of the promised IT park on land later confirmed as Waqf by the 2012 High Court ruling; ownership was subsequently returned to the state government by the 2022 Supreme Court ruling.
cases.court_case: Part of the Manikonda Jagir case (AP High Court 2012 / Supreme Court 2022)
cases.summary: About 100 acres of Dargah Hussain Shah Wali's waqf land was sold by then Chief Minister Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy's government to Lagadapati Rajagopal's Lanco Hills, which was expected to build an IT park but instead constructed premium residential and commercial space.

cases.name: Baba Sharfuddin Dargah, Pahadi Shareef
cases.location: Pahadi Shareef, Balapur, near Shamshabad airport
cases.status: Ongoing. 2023 allegations that encroachers (reportedly linked to a state minister and his son) built two temples and a crematorium on dargah hillside land using JCBs/crushers; in May 2025 the Waqf Board repossessed a separately leased plot at the dargah over unpaid dues of Rs 59.25 lakh.
cases.summary: Of the 5,495 acres identified for Shamshabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, 1,100 acres was gazetted as Waqf land belonging to Dargah Baba Sharfuddin; encroachers allegedly built two temples and a crematorium on the dargah's hillside land over nine years, and the Waqf Board separately reclaimed a leased educational-society plot in 2025 over defaulted dues.

cases.name: Guttala Begumpet land (Masjid Alamgiri)
cases.status: Telangana High Court restored the Waqf gazette notification in favour of Masjid Alamgiri/Waqf Board in 2019; a two-decade dispute with roughly 300 Jubilee Pallavi Enclave families continues, and the Waqf Board acted against fresh encroachment attempts in 2025.
cases.court_case: Addagutta Cooperative Housing Society writ petition; Telangana High Court division bench (CJ Thottathil B. Radhakrishnan and Justice A. Rajasheker Reddy)
cases.summary: 93 acres notified as Waqf land in 1988 (based on a claimed oral Aurangzeb-era gift) has been disputed with private owners since 1995; the Telangana High Court restored the Waqf notification for Masjid Alamgiri in 2019, but around 300 families of Jubilee Pallavi Enclave who bought plots in 1987 remain caught in the legal battle, and the Waqf Board again intervened against encroachment in 2025.

cases.name: Jamia Nizamia land, Raidurg (Survey No. 83/1)
cases.estimated_value_inr: Auctioned at up to Rs 237 crore/acre as part of the Raidurg Knowledge City sale (over Rs 1,490 crore total raised)
cases.status: Ongoing dispute; Jamia Nizamia alleges the land was auctioned by TGIIC despite being recorded and approved as Waqf on the Centre's UMEED portal, and despite pre-auction objections. A judicial probe has been demanded.
cases.court_case: Civil revision petition pending before Telangana High Court; judicial probe demanded by BRS leader Shaik Abdullah Sohail
cases.summary: Jamia Nizamia, one of Hyderabad's oldest Islamic seminaries, says roughly 510 acres of its Waqf land at Raidurg (linked to Dargah Shah Wali/Ghazi Yar Jung endowments) was sold by the Telangana government/TGIIC in its high-value Knowledge City land auction despite written pre-auction objections and the land's Waqf status being verified on the Centre's UMEED portal.

cases.name: Mamidipally waqf land
cases.status: Waqf Board preparing property inventory and hiring senior lawyers ahead of a December 2020 High Court hearing.
cases.summary: About 700 acres of Waqf land at Mamidipally has reportedly been swallowed by land grabbers, according to Telangana State Waqf Board officials in 2020.

cases.name: Balapur waqf land
cases.status: In the clutches of land grabbers per the Waqf Board's 2020 statement; revenue authorities allegedly mutated some parcels to private persons/firms.
cases.summary: About 100 acres of Waqf land at Balapur has reportedly been encroached, with revenue authorities accused of mutating Waqf land to private individuals and companies.

cases.name: Maheswaram Muslim Maternity Hospital land
cases.status: A 2013 CCS case was registered over the alleged illegal sale; as of 2020 reports, roughly 500 acres of the same broader parcel remained with land grabbers.
cases.court_case: Central Crime Station (CCS) case, 2013 - cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy (IPC)
cases.summary: 428 acres of Waqf land at Maheswaram belonging to the Muslim Maternity Hospital was allegedly illegally sold; two former senior Telangana/AP Waqf Board officials and the board's standing counsel were booked and the case transferred to the Central Crime Station in 2013.

cases.name: Kandukur waqf land
cases.status: Reported as encroached in 2020 Waqf Board statements; no further legal action confirmed in sources.
cases.summary: Over 100 acres of Waqf land at Kandukur is reportedly in the clutches of land grabbers, per 2020 Telangana State Waqf Board statements.

cases.name: Dargah Shah Raju Khattal Hussaini land (Kungara Kalan and citywide parcels)
cases.location: Kungara Kalan and multiple survey parcels across Hyderabad/Rangareddy
cases.status: More than 80 cases linked to this dargah's land are pending before the Telangana High Court; the Waqf Board has been criticized for failing to file timely responses in key hearings.
cases.court_case: 80+ cases pending before Telangana High Court
cases.summary: About 400 acres in Kungara Kalan is attached to Dargah Shah Raju Khattal Hussaini, and more broadly over 1,300 acres linked to this dargah are entangled in more than 80 pending Telangana High Court cases, with the Waqf Board repeatedly failing to respond in several hearings.

cases.name: Shamshabad land fraud (forged court orders, waqf-linked prohibited list)
cases.status: Telangana High Court ordered an FIR and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe after discovering forged court orders used to alienate land; a related case involves a former High Court judge challenging inclusion of his Shamshabad land in the Section 22-A 'prohibited' (waqf-linked) property list.
cases.court_case: Telangana High Court order for FIR/SIT probe into Shamshabad land fraud
cases.summary: The Telangana High Court uncovered forged court orders used in a large Shamshabad land scam and ordered an FIR and SIT investigation; separately, a former High Court judge is challenging the inclusion of his Shamshabad land parcel in the Waqf-linked Section 22-A prohibited property list.

cases.name: Ashoorkhana Naal-e-Mubarak land
cases.status: Telangana High Court dismissed a private claimant's petition and upheld the Waqf Board's gazette notifications protecting the land.
cases.court_case: Chenu Radhakrishna vs Telangana State Waqf Board, Telangana High Court
cases.summary: A private individual holding a 2022 sale deed for a plot in Survey No. 219 sought permission to build on land the Waqf Board has repeatedly gazetted as belonging to Ashoorkhana Naal-e-Mubarak; the Telangana High Court ruled that sales of Waqf property are null and void and upheld protection of the 300-acre parcel.

cases.name: Malkajgiri 750-acre waqf claim (Marriott/Park Hyatt area)
cases.status: Registration department suspended property registrations across 100+ survey numbers; backlash reported from roughly 20,000 households across about 100 colonies; hotel properties including Marriott and Park Hyatt reportedly among entangled parcels.
cases.summary: The Telangana Waqf Board's 2024 claim over roughly 750 acres in Malkajgiri triggered suspension of property registrations across more than 100 survey numbers, affecting an estimated 20,000 households in about 100 colonies, with hotel properties such as Marriott and Park Hyatt reportedly caught up in the claim.

cases.name: Property near Muthyallamma temple (Niranjan Bai)
cases.status: Waqf Board issued a notice under the Waqf Act, 1995 against a private resident's property; contested by locals and commentators as an improper claim.
cases.summary: The Telangana Waqf Board issued a notice under the Waqf Act, 1995 asserting a claim over a private resident's (Niranjan Bai) property near the Muthyallamma temple in Secunderabad, prompting local backlash over alleged overreach into non-Waqf private property.

cases.name: Zaheerabad-area farmland (Koheer, Nyalkal, Jharasangham, Raikod mandals)
cases.location: Zaheerabad taluk (Koheer, Nyalkal, Jharasangham, Zaheerabad, Raikod mandals)
cases.status: Farmers report resolution/relief after the 2025 Waqf Amendment Act; earlier, an RTI activist documenting the dispute was assaulted in 2021 despite a High Court status-quo order.
cases.court_case: High Court status-quo order (2021); farmers cite relief following the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025
cases.summary: Around 13,000 acres of farmland across several Zaheerabad-area mandals were recorded as Waqf property after Telangana's 'Dharani' land records system was introduced, leaving long-time pattadar farmers unable to sell land or crops; an RTI activist documenting the issue was assaulted in 2021, and affected farmers publicly thanked MP D.K. Aruna in 2025 after the Waqf Amendment Act.

cases.name: Saidapur village farmland, Survey No. 78
cases.status: Cited by an MP as an unresolved example of pattadar farmland reclassified as Waqf property.
cases.summary: In Survey No. 78 at Saidapur village, Kondapur mandal, roughly 197 acres cultivated by about 200 farmers holding pattadar passbooks was declared Waqf property, cited by BJP MP M. Raghunandan Rao as an example of disputed 'waqf by user' land classifications in Sangareddy district.

cases.name: Kohir waqf land
cases.status: Ongoing, prolonged litigation; land beneficiaries have staged public protests over the contested parcel.
cases.summary: About 3,000 acres at Kohir in Sangareddy district is cited as one of Telangana's high-profile prolonged Waqf litigation zones, alongside Shamshabad airport and Gachibowli/HITEC City land, with Waqf land beneficiaries protesting over the dispute.

cases.name: Toli Masjid waqf land
cases.status: Long-running encroachment since at least 2006; a 2017 High Court order to remove encroachments was never implemented; an activist campaigning against the encroachment was violently attacked.
cases.court_case: High Court order (2017) directing removal of encroachments, reportedly unimplemented
cases.summary: Of the 27 acres of Waqf land attached to the 17th-century Toli Masjid near Golconda Fort, about 17 acres have been encroached, including an illegally built function hall (Mahboob Pride Palace, on which an FIR was filed); Deccan Waqf Protection Society president Osman Bin Alhajri was left critically injured in an attack for pursuing the case, and his son was also attacked.

cases.name: Golconda Eidgah land
cases.status: Attempted temple construction on the Eidgah's waqf land was reported and opposed.
cases.summary: An attempt to construct a temple on Waqf land belonging to the Golconda Eidgah was reported by local media and opposed by community members.

cases.name: Koudi Shah Graveyard
cases.status: Shops (a 'malgi' commercial structure) built on graveyard land, and decades-old police quarters/police station occupy part of the site; a 2025 Waqf Board site inspection produced no confirmed follow-up action.
cases.summary: The centuries-old Koudi Shah Graveyard in Aliabad, spread over more than two acres, has been encroached by shop construction with alleged support from local leaders, and by police quarters and a police station built decades ago; when asked for a case follow-up in 2025, the Waqf Board chairperson said he was 'not aware of such a case.'

cases.name: Oontwadi Graveyard (Qabristan Chudi Bazaar)
cases.status: Neglected and misused; no remediation reported.
cases.summary: The 3,300-square-yard Oontwadi Graveyard (Qabristan Chudi Bazaar) in Jummerat Bazaar has fallen into official neglect and is being used as a stable for camels and horses, with carts and animal waste littering the burial ground.

cases.name: Rahmath Nagar graveyard land dispute (Waqf Board vs Defence Ministry)
cases.status: Graveyard construction plan dropped after Army objection; matter referred to the district collector for re-verification; government explored an alternate site at Erragadda.
cases.summary: The Telangana Waqf Board's plan to build a graveyard on about 2,500 square yards (22,500 sq ft) in Rahmath Nagar, Jubilee Hills, was halted after the Indian Army said the land belonged to the Defence Ministry and housed military workshops/warehouses; the plan was dropped amid a politically charged dispute ahead of the Jubilee Hills by-election, and an alternate site at Erragadda was considered.

cases.name: Asmangadh / Malakpet waqf land
cases.location: Asmangadh, Malakpet (Mumtaz College area) and adjoining Mallepally
cases.status: Disputed; multiple cases pending before Waqf authorities/tribunals. The advocate pursuing these cases, Khaja Moizuddin, was killed near Masab Tank in an attack police suspect is linked to the Waqf land disputes he was litigating.
cases.court_case: Multiple pending disputes before Waqf tribunals/authorities pursued by advocate Khaja Moizuddin
cases.summary: About 36 acres of Waqf land at Asmangadh in Malakpet (where Mumtaz College and other institutions sit), along with adjoining land near Anwar-ul-Uloom Degree College in Mallepally, have been the subject of alleged illegal occupation and privatization by individuals claiming mutawalli status; advocate Khaja Moizuddin, who litigated these cases, was killed in a suspected targeted attack in 2025.

cases.name: Qutub Shahi Masjid and Dargah Saadullah Hussaini land (Secretariat Enclave)
cases.location: Neknampur, Gandipet (Secretariat Enclave, behind the Seven Tombs)
cases.status: Recurring pattern since 2012: excavation/encroachment attempts are reported, police intervene and work stops temporarily, then debris is cleared overnight before authorities can document it; most recently flagged in February 2024.
cases.summary: Heritage activist Ilyas Khan (Heritage Watch) has repeatedly flagged excavation using heavy machinery on land around the 400-year-old Qutub Shahi Masjid and the adjoining Dargah Saadullah Hussaini graveyard near the Seven Tombs in Neknampur/Gandipet, describing a pattern of encroachment attempts recurring since 2012.

cases.name: Narketpally mosque-adjacent land
cases.status: Tension defused by police in January 2024; no temple construction was permitted at the time.
cases.summary: In January 2024, a mob of 200-250 people from right-wing groups (VHP, Bajrang Dal, RSS, BJP) gathered on a 2,840-square-yard Waqf-registered open plot beside a mosque in Narketpally, Nalgonda district, attempting to construct a Hanuman temple, prompting police intervention.

cases.name: Brahmamgaru Gutta ghat road land
cases.estimated_value_inr: Rs 140 crore (value of the stalled road project)
cases.status: Rs 140-crore ghat road project to the Durga Devi Temple/BrahmamGari Math stalled indefinitely after the Waqf Board refused to issue a No Objection Certificate, citing ownership under the Waqf Act, 1995 (letter dated July 9, 2025), despite the project having cleared departmental approvals and reached the tendering stage.
cases.summary: A state government-backed Rs 140 crore ghat road to the Durga Devi Temple and BrahmamGari Math atop Brahmamgaru Gutta in Nalgonda district was halted after the Telangana Waqf Board claimed ownership of the land and denied the required NOC.

cases.name: Dargah Hazrat Yakoob Shaheed, Annaram
cases.status: Writ petition pending/heard before the Telangana High Court over the Waqf Board's notification to auction offering-collection rights at the dargah, following a lease-extension dispute tied to pandemic-era closures.
cases.court_case: Mohammed Altaf Hussain vs Telangana State Waqf Board (writ petition), Telangana High Court
cases.summary: A writ petition before the Telangana High Court challenged the Waqf Board's move to auction collection rights at Dargah Hazrat Yakoob Shaheed in Annaram, Warangal district, after the petitioner's request to extend his lease (due to pandemic closures cutting off revenue) was contested by the Board.

cases.name: Dargah Hzt. Syed Shaheed Habeeb Ullah (RH)
cases.status: Telangana High Court admitted, then ultimately rejected, a writ petition challenging the constitution of the dargah's managing committee.
cases.court_case: Mohammed Abdul Rafi & others vs constitution of dargah managing committee, Telangana High Court (Justice Surepalli Nanda)
cases.summary: Petitioners challenged a March 13 order constituting a new managing committee for Dargah Hzt. Syed Shaheed Habeeb Ullah (RH) and its associated graveyard and chillas (Chillah Zinda Shah Madar, Chillah Saad Ullah Hussaini) in Nizamabad district, alleging the move was politically influenced and disregarded their pending claim to continue in office; the High Court ultimately rejected the petition.
